narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Creon forbids burial of Polyneices after the attack on Thebes. Antigone defies him in the name of obligations to her brother and the gods. The play tests Creon’s assertion of civic authority against duties his decree cannot simply erase.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translation; whitespace normalized): “vengeance with his kinsmen’s blood, Or drag them captive at his chariot wheels— For Polyneices ’tis ordained that none Shall give him burial or make mourn for him, But leave his corpse unburied, to be meat For dogs and carrion crows, a ghastly sight. So am I purposed; never by my will Shall miscreants”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Antigone says she follows unwritten divine laws rather than a mortal decree; the play stages the conflict and its consequences.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: Separate Creon’s justification of his decree from the play’s testing of that justification. Noticing competing claims does not require treating every character’s position as equally defensible.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: A hero can be right about a duty and still help produce catastrophe.
